what: The source (World Bank, 2024-04-05, Box 11 "Regulations and Initiatives Led by CBY-Aden to Improve Payment Systems in Yemen", line 6682) gives one direction only: "PSPs in Sana’a face encouraging results but are not authorized to operate in Aden without investing in separate infrastructures located in the South." what: The cited part rests on ACAPS of 2026-10-10 (YE-E1307, YE-E1308: "Old banknotes are used in the de-facto authority (DFA) areas in the north of Yemen (also known as the Houthis)"), grouped in Houthis' area; no state at that place is later (Houthi-controlled areas is another place group). Q1:131's "differ by area" rests on the same quote's "new banknotes are used in the Internationally Recognized Government (IRG) controlled south and east of Yemen" and the record's IRG-area part.

The quote is Wise's currency converter, "Convert YER to USD at the mid-market exchange rate" and "1 USD = 236.197 YER" (2026-10-10), place not stated; the other states at place not stated (251, 2017-09; 236.15, 2026-10-09) are earlier. The points say only that this quote differs from both cities' market rates; that it rules out a rate source (Q7:135) is the proposal's reasoning.

The state at the internationally recognized government's area bars foreign currency in domestic transactions (YE-E410, 2026-04-24: "enforce the use of the rial in all domestic transactions"; YE-E443: "The government also prohibited the use of foreign currency for all commercial and service transactions and financial contracts.") but says nothing of showing prices in a foreign currency, so Q7:136's "a foreign currency can only be a shown-only currency there" says what the evidence at that place doesn't. Q1:132, Q4:135, Q4:151 and Q8:184 hold; no later state at that place.
